questions.question: Which command prints the current working directory?
questions.explanation: pwd prints the absolute path of the current directory.

questions.question: Which command lists all files, including hidden ones, in long format?
questions.explanation: -l gives long format and -a includes dotfiles.

questions.question: Which command displays the last 10 lines of a file by default?
questions.explanation: tail prints the last 10 lines unless -n says otherwise.

questions.question: Which command searches files for lines matching a text pattern?
questions.explanation: grep prints lines matching a pattern; find searches for files by attributes.

questions.question: What does cd .. do?
questions.explanation: .. refers to the parent of the current directory.

questions.question: Which command creates nested directories a/b/c, without error if they already exist?
questions.explanation: -p creates missing parents and does not fail on existing directories.

questions.question: Which command shows the manual page for ls?
questions.explanation: man displays the manual page for a command.

questions.question: Which operator redirects stdout to a file, appending instead of overwriting?
questions.explanation: >> appends; > truncates the file first.

questions.question: Which permission string results from chmod 754 file?
questions.explanation: 7=rwx for owner, 5=r-x for group, 4=r-- for others.

questions.question: A file shows -rw-r----- in ls -l. Apart from root, who can read it?
options: The owner and members of the file's group
questions.explanation: Owner has rw-, group has r--, others have no permissions.

questions.question: Which command makes alice the owner and dev the group of file?
questions.explanation: chown user:group sets both owner and group.

questions.question: In cmd > out.log 2>&1, what does 2>&1 do?
options: Redirects stderr to where stdout points, so both go to out.log
questions.explanation: 2>&1 duplicates file descriptor 1 onto 2 after stdout has been pointed at out.log.

questions.question: Which command lists all processes of all users with details such as user, CPU and memory?
questions.explanation: ps aux shows every process in BSD-style user-oriented format.

questions.question: Which signal does kill PID send when no signal is specified?
questions.explanation: kill sends SIGTERM (15) by default, allowing the process to clean up.

questions.question: What does find /var/log -name "*.log" -mtime -1 return?
options: .log files under /var/log older than one day
.log files under /var/log modified less than 24 hours ago
questions.explanation: -mtime -1 matches files modified within the last 24 hours.

questions.question: Which command shows free and used space of mounted filesystems in human-readable units?
questions.explanation: df reports filesystem usage; du measures directory sizes and free shows memory.

questions.question: What is the effect of the setgid bit on a directory?
options: New files created inside inherit the directory's group
Files inside run with the owner's privileges
Only root can create files inside
questions.explanation: On directories, setgid makes new entries inherit the directory's group ownership.

questions.question: What does the sticky bit on /tmp (drwxrwxrwt) do?
options: Lets only a file's owner, the directory's owner or root delete or rename it
questions.explanation: Without it, anyone with write access to the directory could delete others' files.

questions.question: With umask 022, what mode does a newly created regular file get by default?
questions.explanation: Files start from 666; masking out 022 gives 644 (rw-r--r--).

questions.question: In cmd1 && cmd2 || cmd3, what happens if cmd1 fails?
options: cmd2 runs but cmd3 does not
cmd3 runs and cmd2 is skipped
questions.explanation: && skips cmd2 on failure; the list then has a non-zero status, so || runs cmd3.

questions.question: Which command adds execute permission on deploy.sh for its owner only, leaving other bits unchanged?
questions.explanation: u+x changes only the user's execute bit; +x and a+x affect everyone and 700 replaces all bits.

questions.question: A hard link and a symbolic link both point to file f. What happens after rm f?
options: The hard link still accesses the data; the symlink becomes dangling
The symlink still works; the hard link breaks
questions.explanation: A hard link is another name for the same inode; a symlink stores a path that no longer exists.
